what_this_is: Two bounded things: Cincinnati's Hilton acquisition finished, and a controlled one-shot retry of the five Marriott rows pilot 014 lost to a challenge page. Nine attempts, one lane, no escalation, no second retry.

authorization.two_independent_gates: a controlled retry had to be authorised TWICE and was: the paid ledger suppresses an already-bought page (--material-changes, OPERATOR_OVERRIDE) and the retry policy suppresses a same-lane retry (--retry-overrides). A control run with the ledger authorisation withheld left 4 payable rows and suppressed 5, which is how we know both gates were load-bearing rather than decorative.

spend.note: the zone meter's delta ($1.45) and the runner's estimate ($1.44) agree almost exactly; the prepaid balance lags and was still settling when last read. Every meter is under the cap.

correction_to_pilot_014.what_014_reported: $1.08 measured, and a sizing rate of $0.09 per attempt
correction_to_pilot_014.what_settled: the prepaid balance fell from $8.34 to $6.44 across pilot 014 and the interval before this run, and the zone month-to-date rose $2.61 over the same window -- both materially more than $1.08.
correction_to_pilot_014.why_it_matters: pilot 014 priced the remaining Marriott cohort at $0.09 per attempt and therefore UNDERSTATED it by roughly 44%. Any plan built on that figure is too cheap.
correction_to_pilot_014.caveat: the vendor's meters are account-wide and cannot be attributed to a single run with certainty. $0.16 is used because it is the conservative reading, not because it is provably this market's cost.

the_statistical_honesty: Retry access 4/5 and first-attempt access 3/8 have OVERLAPPING Wilson intervals ([0.376, 0.964] against [0.137, 0.694]). The rates alone therefore do not establish that retrying helps, and this order does not claim they do. The finding that carries weight is mechanical: ZERO of the five challenges repeated. A per-property block would have reproduced on the same URL; none did. The single miss was ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED at zero bytes -- a transport failure that never reached Marriott and cannot testify about a bot wall in either direction.

marriott_recommendation.policy: at most two browser attempts per property: the first, and one retry if and only if the first was challenged
marriott_recommendation.why: none of the 5 challenges repeated on retry, which a property-specific block would have done, and 4 of 5 retries reached the page. Two-attempt access is 0.875 against one-attempt access of 0.375.
marriott_recommendation.what_would_change_it: a repeated challenge rate above zero at scale. Five rows cannot prove it stays zero, so the scale-up must measure it again rather than assume this held.

hilton_final.why_closed: every routed unresolved Hilton identity in Cincinnati has now been attempted; zero remain. This is an exhausted population, not a sample, which is a stronger statement than any interval.
hilton_final.the_one_miss: The Cincinnatian returned a complete page that publishes no pet policy. That is the hotel's answer, not the lane's failure.

application_inventory.applied: NOTHING. This order measured and acquired. No record was written, no identity resolved, no exclusion registered, no route changed.

preserved_questions.fee_or_deposit: All SEVEN publication-grade Hilton rows carry 'Deposit Yes. $X Non-refundable Fee'. Order 015 does NOT resolve it -- if anything the opposite: the phrasing is identical across seven properties, which shows it is a Hilton template artifact rather than seven independent statements. A deposit and a non-refundable fee are two different charges and this label names both.
preserved_questions.homewood_tier_gap: Still unresolved, and order 015 supplies positive evidence that inferring it would have been WRONG. Homewood reads '$75.00(1-nights), $125.00(5+nights)'. Its siblings do not agree with each other: Florence, Milford, Mason and Spark use 1-4/5+, while SHARONVILLE uses 1-3nts/4-7nts. There is no single sibling ladder to borrow, so nights 2-4 stay unstated.

The retry died on ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED with zero bytes -- the transport never reached Marriott. It is neither a repeated challenge nor an answer, and the row is simply still open.

binding_constraint.finding: two properties share ONE block digest
binding_constraint.why: both refusals are the identical 27-character string 'Pet Policy Pets Not Allowed', so hashing the BLOCK hashes the sentence, not the hotel. Fourteen blocks produce only thirteen distinct block digests.
binding_constraint.rule: an approval must bind document_sha256, never block_sha256 alone. The page digests are distinct 14 of 14; the block digests are not, and a record bound to a shared block digest names evidence that could have come from either building.

remaining_marriott.derivation: rebuilt from the routing shard, the partition and the paid ledger; not quoted from a prior report

projection.why_the_ceiling: the cap is set at two attempts for every row, which is the most the policy can ever spend. Sizing a cap at the EXPECTED number of attempts guarantees the run stops halfway the first time access is worse than the sample.

balance_warning.what_this_means: the full 34-row scale-up cannot be funded from the current balance. It needs either a top-up before it starts or splitting into batches, and a run that discovers this halfway through leaves the cohort stranded mid-population.
